name: Davide Scaramuzza

papers.title: Learning Visuomotor Quadrotor Flight Through Dynamic Narrow Gaps
papers.abstract: Threading a quadrotor through a moving narrow gap is a demanding test of agile flight, requiring centimeter-level spatial alignment and precise temporal execution. We address this challenge in a purely state-free setting, where a control policy operates directly on onboard visual and inertial measurements to output collective thrust and body-rate commands. The task is difficult because success lies on a thin feasible manifold: small errors in timing, position, attitude, or visual observability cause collision. Prior planning and learning methods rely on privileged state, teachers, planners, or distillation; learning dynamic narrow-gap traversal directly, from scratch, remains open. We introduce a differentiable simulation framework that trains visual-inertial, observation-to-command policies entirely from random initialization. By backpropagating through differentiable quadrotor dynamics and smooth task costs, our approach constitutes the first method to learn dynamic narrow-gap traversal without relying on a teacher, planner, or distillation. We validate our approach in both synthetic and real-world experiments. In controlled benchmarks, we demonstrate that pathwise gradients significantly outperform score-function gradients for precision-critical tasks, yielding a 99.3% success rate in simulation after only a few minutes of training on a single GPU. Furthermore, the policy transfers directly to a real quadrotor, successfully crossing a dynamic narrow gap from varied initial conditions using exclusively onboard sensing, achieving an 80% success rate over 10 physical trials.

papers.title: Approximate Imitation Learning for Event-based Quadrotor Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers.abstract: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low latency, making them ideal sensors for high-speed robotic applications where conventional cameras suffer from image degradations such as motion blur. In addition, their low power consumption can enhance endurance, which is critical for resource-constrained platforms. Motivated by these properties, we present a novel approach that enables a quadrotor to fly through cluttered environments at high speed by perceiving the environment with a single event camera. Our proposed method employs an end-to-end neural network trained to map event data directly to control commands, eliminating the reliance on standard cameras. To enable efficient training in simulation, where rendering synthetic event data is computationally expensive, we propose Approximate Imitation Learning, a novel imitation learning framework. Our approach leverages a large-scale offline dataset to learn a task-specific representation space. Subsequently, the policy is trained through online interactions that rely solely on lightweight, simulated state information, eliminating the need to render events during training. This enables the efficient training of event-based control policies for fast quadrotor flight, highlighting the potential of our framework for other modalities where data simulation is costly or impractical. Our approach outperforms standard imitation learning baselines in simulation and demonstrates robust performance in real-world flight tests, achieving speeds up to 9.8ms^-1 in cluttered environments.
